pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:1 The workflow calls itself the merge rung, but nothing in the repository reads back or records which of its check names the merge decision requires; a tracked-file search for protection, required-check, ruleset and gh-api readback found nothing, so a renamed job (for example 'web (tokens, contract, packages, stage, console)') could stop binding merges with no gate going red.

techniques.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:1 No readback of required checks and no committed expected-binding text. The join is by job name, and the workflow also runs on push to main, where it reports after the fact rather than refusing.

README.md:56 This hand-written projection understates the enforced set. `node scripts/ci-lanes.mjs --check` today prints '22 lanes derived, 22 covered', and ci.yml runs a 4th Python suite (avatar3d, line 238) that README lines 49-51 omit.

eslint.config.js:54 The keyboard-listener ban only matches a literal first argument. addEventListener(evt, f) with a variable, or JSON reached via an alias or via globalThis.JSON.parse, evades the rule silently instead of the unrecognised form being refused, although the repo owns the tree.
.github/workflows/ci.yml:75 Warnings are promoted to errors in the invocation itself, so the exit code carries them.
.github/workflows/ci.yml:77 A zero-test floor turns an emptied lane into a failure instead of a green.
.github/workflows/ci.yml:42 The toolchain and actions are pinned, so blocking verdicts are a function of the commit. No external-feed audit step blocks.
.github/workflows/ci.yml:14 The gate population is derived from pnpm-workspace and package scripts, not a hand list, and the check fails on uncovered or stale lanes.
README.md:39 Every local gate also exists on the clean-room rung. The fidelity gate is explicitly local-only (ci.yml:10), which makes it a courtesy, not a gate.
.github/workflows/ci.yml:209 The size cap and token rules are mechanised and run at merge, not left as prose.
eslint.config.js:11 The partition (lint without types; types owned by the tsc typecheck lanes) is written down, not hidden.
eslint.config.js:33 Verified that apps/console/src/keys/keymap.ts exists, and that the JSON.parse remedy (parseRpcResult/parseEvent) is exported by packages/contract/src/index.ts.
eslint.config.js:9 Each suppression is keyed to a file and rule id with a count, not a blanket waiver.
eslint.config.js:149 A detector that misfires on correct code is narrowed with its reason stated, not bypassed ad hoc.

pairs.registryProposal: unparseable-form-is-a-finding is framed around matchers without a parser, but AST-selector bans (eslint no-restricted-syntax keyed on a literal argument or an identifier name) share the same open escape set (non-literal argument, aliasing, globalThis.X). The technique could name AST-selector rules as an in-scope middle case.

pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: apps/console/src/pages/reconcile/model.ts:103 The page re-implements the daemon's constitution refusal with its own narrower predicate. The daemon's verify.rs:90 uses a lowercased contains('constitution.md') over headers and body lines, while the console uses an anchored regex over header paths only. So the surface that refuses an option ('Cannot be chosen') is a hand-walked subset of the enforced policy, not a projection of the daemon's verdict.

techniques.evidence: apps/console/src/pages/reconcile/model.ts:103 This is a second authority for the immutable-constitution rule. It diverges from crates/shadowrunr-reconcile/src/verify.rs:90/195 instead of rendering a flag the verifier emits.
apps/console/src/pages/reconcile/model.ts:72 Rates below the sample floor are counted and announced, and 'unmeasured' is its own verdict label (line 157), not a zero.

pairs.registryProposal: policy-projection could name the client-side duplicate of a server-side refusal predicate (a defence-in-depth UI block) as a projection class: the fix is to carry the enforcer's verdict to the surface, not to re-derive it.
